pages.text: The Energy Generator is your $(4)entry-level standalone generator$(0): feed it Akaishi fuel and it burns steadily at a base rate of $(bold)75 AE/tick$(0) (AE = Akaishi Energy).$(br2)$(bold)Boosting it:$(0)it has 10 upgrade slots. Each Energy Production Upgrade Component is ×1.75 output (with a 1% output tax), so $(4)a full rack lands around ×242$(0).$(br2)$(bold)Five fuel tiers$(0) (heating value):$(li)Akaishi Crystal: 2000$(li)Raw Akaishi Block: 20000$(li)Akaishi Essence: 80000$(li)Condensed Akaishi Essence: 800000$(li)Condensed Akaishi Essence Block: 7200000$(br2)Where those fuels come from and how to refine them: "$(l:akaishi:energy_basics)Akaishi Energy Basics$(/l)". One unit too weak? The upgrade path is the "$(l:akaishi:gen_matrix)Akaishi Generator Matrix$(/l)".

$(bold)Retired builds:$(0) the $(4)Small Assembly$(0) (3×3×3) and the $(4)Super Generator$(0) (5×5×5) block-built forms have $(bold)retired$(0). The Akaishi Generator Matrix now does that job, and the old blocks are just $(e)spare parts$(0).$(br2)$(bold)Standalone vs matrix:$(0) the generator is cheap, drop-in and carries its own fuel slot; $(4)the matrix needs grid power$(0), but starts at a ×45 multiplier — your budget and line size decide which route to take.$(br2)Forming requirements and both tiers' stats live in the "$(l:akaishi:gen_matrix)Akaishi Generator Matrix$(/l)" entry.

Suggested reading: start with "$(l:akaishi:energy_basics)Akaishi Energy Basics$(/l)" to master fuel, then wire everything up with "$(l:akaishi:energy_pipe)Energy Pipes$(/l)" and "$(l:akaishi:energy_cell)Energy Cells$(/l)"; to scale up, build the "$(l:akaishi:gen_matrix)Generator Matrix$(/l)" — and when even that falls short, it's time for the "$(l:akaishi:reactor)Reactor$(/l)".
